data.name: Beyond: Two Souls
data.detailed_description:
O talento e narrativa de grande nível trazem-te uma experiência com um videojogo como nunca antes tiveste.

VIVE UMA VIDA EXTRAORDINÁRIA: UMA VIDA, DUAS ALMAS


Um thriller de ação psicológico apresentado com atuações dos grandes atores de Hollywood Elliot Page e Willem Dafoe, Beyond: Two Souls™ leva-te numa viagem emocionante por todo o mundo, enquanto desvendas a vida extraordinária de Jodie Holmes.

A Jodie é diferente, nasceu com uma ligação com uma entidade misteriosa com poderes incríveis.

As tuas ações vão determinar o destino de Jodie enquanto ela enfrenta desafios extraordinários, perigos e perdas de partir o coração numa viagem para descobrir a verdade sobre quem ela é.

Cria uma história cheia de ação através das tuas escolhas e atos enquanto vives a sua vida - uma rapariga que nasceu com uma ligação com uma entidade sobrenatural chamada Aiden.

Ao jogares como a Jodie e o Aiden, vais enfrentar desafios físicos e psicológicos espetaculares para compreender o que realmente está... além.

TESTA AS TUAS HABILIDADES COM "EXPERIÊNCIAS AVANÇADAS"

A missão original de DLC dos lançamentos para PlayStation™ está incluída no jogo completo para PC. Podes jogar todo o jogo em dois modos de dificuldade e nos modos Solo ou Duo.

JOGA A HISTÓRIA COMO QUISERES

Em ordem cinemática ou cronológica? Escolhe a forma como queres viver a história e joga até em modo cooperativo local, com dois comandos diferentes para cada jogador - um para jogar como a Jodie e o outro para jogar como o Aiden. Joga à tua maneira.

COMPLETAMENTE OTIMIZADO PARA PC

Beyond: Two Souls chega aos PCs com visuais deslumbrantes que incluem a resolução 4K, compatível com monitores ultrawide 21:9 e de 60 fotogramas por segundo.

reviews.review:
[h3]Sometimes, All You Want Is a Normal Life[/h3]
Some games stay on your wishlist for years, even when you don't really know when you'll finally get around to playing them. [b]Beyond: Two Souls[/b] was one of those games for me. I had never played it on console, but it had always been somewhere in the back of my mind. Then I saw it for €0.99, and I thought it was finally time to give it a chance. I certainly don't regret it.

I went into the game knowing almost nothing about its story. I knew Elliot Page was in it, but I had no idea Willem Dafoe was part of the cast too, which was a very welcome surprise. I wanted to discover the story for myself, without knowing where it would lead or what I should expect. And I'm glad I did, because there are moments here that work best when you experience them without any prior knowledge.

[h3]Jodie and Aiden: Two Souls, One Journey[/h3]
I played through the game twice: first in its original narrative order, then again in chronological order, with a second run that also became my own little solo co-op adventure. I really enjoyed both versions. Experiencing the same events in a different order gave me another perspective on Jodie's life, and I appreciated being able to see her journey both as it was originally presented and as a more continuous story.

The relationship between Jodie and Aiden is the heart of the experience. At first, I saw Aiden as a protective companion, always there when Jodie needed help. I never really found him unsettling; I simply accepted him as a strange and mysterious presence that was part of her life. Then came the moment when I discovered who Aiden really was. That revelation caught me completely off guard, and I honestly felt my heart melt. I won't say anything more about it, because it's one of those moments that deserves to be experienced firsthand.

Playing as Aiden was also something I genuinely enjoyed. The first time I discovered how his abilities worked, being pulled away from Jodie and suddenly floating through the air and space around her felt completely unexpected. I had no idea the game would let me experience the world from such a different perspective, and that sense of discovery stayed with me.

[h3]Growing Up with Jodie[/h3]
I found myself especially connected to Jodie during her childhood and pre-teen years. I wanted to help her, protect her and guide her through situations that were often far too complicated for someone so young. Her life is full of moments in which she is forced to face things she doesn't fully understand, while the people around her don't always know how to deal with what makes her different. I felt responsible for my choices, as though I were trying to give her a little help along the way. Of course, I couldn't always get everything right, but that's part of the experience.

What touched me most was not simply the supernatural side of her story, but the very human need underneath it all. Jodie wants to be accepted. She wants to belong. She wants to experience the world without constantly feeling different from everyone else. And sometimes, all she wants is to be able to live the kind of life that other people take for granted.

I also grew very fond of Nathan Dawkins and Cole Freeman. In many ways, they felt like surrogate parents to Jodie, and I often found myself empathizing with them just as much as, and sometimes even more than, with Jodie herself. Their presence gave her life some much-needed stability, even when everything around her seemed uncertain. Ryan, on the other hand, was someone I never fully trusted at first. As the story progressed, though, I came to understand his role and appreciate what he brought to Jodie's journey.

[h3]A Story That Feels Like an Interactive Film[/h3]
[b]Beyond: Two Souls[/b] worked for me precisely because I approached it as an interactive film. I wasn't looking for a traditional action game or a world full of systems to master. I wanted to follow a story, make decisions and feel involved in the life of its protagonist. And that's exactly what I got.

The choices made me feel responsible for Jodie's path, even though playing through the story again made me realize that many decisions change individual scenes or details rather than completely rewriting the whole narrative. The biggest differences come through the endings, and I appreciated having several different ways to bring Jodie's story to a close. I also enjoyed seeing how the experience could change depending on whether I was controlling Jodie or Aiden. There was something genuinely fun about switching perspectives and discovering what each of them could do.

The performances are another strong part of the game. Elliot Page brings a great deal of humanity to Jodie, while Willem Dafoe's presence adds even more weight to the cast. The atmosphere is beautiful, shifting between intimate and unsettling moments without losing sight of the emotional core of the story. The soundtrack isn't something I would call unforgettable on its own, but it supports the scenes well and helps carry the mood when the story needs it.

[h3]Choosing What Comes After[/h3]
The different endings were one of my favorite parts of the experience. I enjoyed most of them, but the path where Jodie chooses life was the one that resonated with me the most. After everything she has been through, there is something deeply meaningful about the possibility of continuing to live, to discover what comes next and to find a place in the world.

The other possibilities are interesting too, especially the more unusual choice involving the Beyond. It gives the story a different perspective on what it means to continue existing and on the connections that can remain between people. The glimpse of the possible future is mysterious, and it leaves questions hanging in the air, but what mattered most to me was the choice at the heart of these endings: what kind of future does Jodie want for herself?

After two playthroughs and around 20 hours, I completed every achievement. I did use a guide to make sure I didn't miss anything, because achievement hunting is part of what I enjoy about games. For me, it doesn't take away from the experience. Quite the opposite: there is a particular satisfaction in knowing that I've explored everything I wanted to see and can finally say I've completed the journey.

[h3]Final Thoughts[/h3]
What I will remember most about [b]Beyond: Two Souls[/b] is Jodie.

Not just the person she becomes, but the little girl she was.

The girl who wanted to be understood.

The girl who wanted to be accepted.

The girl who sometimes had to face a world that seemed to have no place for her.

I found myself empathizing with her because, even without anything supernatural, I believe that some children grow up carrying feelings like these. Loneliness. Helplessness. The need to belong somewhere, to be seen for who they are and to have someone stand beside them when life becomes too difficult.

And that is what makes Jodie's story so human to me.

Behind all the mystery, all the extraordinary events and everything that makes her life different, there is a simple wish that almost anyone can understand.

She wants to live.

She wants to be happy.

She wants to have a future.

She wants to make her own choices.

She wants to find the people who will accept her, stay with her and love her for who she is.

In the end, she is not asking for something extraordinary.

She is asking for something that should never have to be extraordinary in the first place...

A normal life.
